description.value: In this assessment, students complete an examination that assesses their understanding of key commercial design principles. The exam includes questions on how designers analyse needs and opportunities, consider ethical and sustainability factors, and apply innovation and enterprise skills when developing commercial products. Students demonstrate knowledge of materials, systems, and manufacturing considerations, as well as basic business concepts such as target audiences, market needs, and value creation. This assessment focuses on students’ ability to explain and apply foundational commercial design knowledge to authentic product design contexts.

conditions.value:
• up to 90 minutes plus 10 minutes planning time

duration.value: up to 90 minutes plus 10 minutes planning time

resourcesAvailable.value: Curated commercial design case studies and Life Cycle Analysis (LCA) tools. Strategic planning frameworks including SWOT analysis, Business Model Canvas, and User Persona templates. Technical stimulus materials, practice examination papers, and revision guides focused on authentic product design scenarios and commercial viability.

instructions.value:
Read all questions and stimulus material carefully during the 10-minute planning time. 
Answer all questions in the provided response booklet.

Section 1: Multiple Choice
• Select the most appropriate response for each question.
• Questions focus on material properties, industrial manufacturing processes, and fundamental commercial design terminology.

Section 2: Short Response
• Provide concise explanations of how designers identify market gaps and respond to specific target audience needs.
• Explain the ethical and environmental implications of material selection using Life Cycle Thinking (LCT) and sustainability frameworks.
• Define and apply business concepts, including value propositions, economic viability, and the role of enterprise skills in product development.

Section 3: Extended Response
• Analyse the provided design scenario to identify an authentic commercial opportunity and define specific user requirements.
• Propose a designed solution that demonstrates innovation and market readiness.
• Justify design decisions by evaluating the proposed solution against social, ethical, economic, and sustainability factors.
• Use professional design terminology and, where appropriate, annotated graphical representations to communicate technical design intent.

context.value: In this unit, students explore commercial design by examining how products are developed to meet user needs and succeed in competitive markets. Students investigate market analysis, target audiences, product design and manufacturing processes, and basic business principles such as value proposition, cost, and sustainability. Through analysis of existing commercial products and innovation case studies, students develop an understanding of how designers balance functionality, aesthetics, ethical considerations, and commercial viability. The unit emphasises innovation, enterprise skills, and informed decision-making in the development of market-ready designed solutions.

authenticationStrategies.label: You will be provided class time for task completion.
You will produce sections of the final response under supervised conditions.
You will provide documentation of your progress.
Your teacher will collect copies of your response and monitor at key junctures.
Your teacher will collect and annotate a draft.
Your teacher will conduct interviews or consultations as you develop the response.
You must submit a declaration of authenticity.
You will produce summaries during your response preparation.
Your teacher will conduct interviews after submission to clarify or explore aspects of your response.
Your teacher will compare the responses of students who have worked together in groups.
Your teacher will ensure class cross-marking occurs.
